frozen_problem.title: A quantitative Borel-Cantelli estimate for VWA matrices
frozen_problem.statement:
Conjecture 24 for compact Γ \G and the measure νT as above with summation taken over regular flats F such that systol( F ) < T. Another equidistribution result was obtained in a recent work of Y. Benoist and H. Oh, where the averages along Hecke orbits of maximal compact flats were considered. 5. Diophantine analysis

5.1. A vector y = ( y1,..., y n) ∈ Rn is called v-approximable (for v > 0) if there are infinitely many q = ( q1,..., q n) ∈ Zn and p ∈ Z such that

|y1q1 + · · · + ynqn − p| < ‖q‖−v.

Here ‖ · ‖ denotes the max-norm on Rn. If a vector y ∈ Rn is ( n + ε)-approximable for some ε > 0, it is called very well approximable (VWA). An easy argument (using Borel-Cantelli lemma) implies that the set of VWA vectors has Lebesgue measure zero in Rn. Therefore, it is natural to expect that a generic point on a "nondegenerate" submanifold of Rn is not VWA. This is the Sprindˇ zuk conjecture proved in [109] (see also [17]). Similarly, an m × n real matrix A is called VWA if for some ε > 0 there are infinitely many q ∈ Zn and p ∈ Zm such that

‖Aq − p‖m < ‖q‖−n−ε.

It is easy to see that the set of VWA matrices has measure zero in Rm×n, and one hopes that an analog of the Sprindˇ zuk conjecture holds in this set-up as well. The definition of nondegenerate submanifold of Rn in [109], which is well-suited for the case of vectors, is a manifold with smooth coordinate charts

f: U (⊂ Rk) → Rn such that the spaces spanned by the partial derivatives f at OPEN PROBLEMS 12

points of U have dimension n. It is not quite clear what is the right definition of "nondegenerate" submanifold for the case of matrices.

theory.target: Reindex the scalar approximation tail by reduced fractions without losing low-denominator exceptions, and sharpen the SAME R=4,K=32 prefix tail certificate using only the primes 2 and 3.
definitions: E_q={x in [0,1]:dist(qx,Z)<q^-2}, q>=2; U(R,K) is its finite union measure.
a/d is reduced, including both endpoints for d=1; q_d=d*ceil(R/d) is its first allowed representative.
phi(q) counts reduced interior centers for q>1; w(q)=(1-1_{2|q}/2)(1-1_{3|q}/3).
B(K) uses signed divisor-tail integral bounds; C(K) uses six convex midpoint integrals.
The packet preserves strict event inequalities but interval-span certificates are measure-equivalent closures.
assumptions: Lebesgue measure on [0,1]; R>=2,K>=R are integers. E_q={x:distance(q*x,Z)<q^-2}; q is positive. Negative q duplicate these events.
All inequalities in event membership are strict. Interval endpoint changes do not affect measure, but pointwise counterexamples retain strict endpoints.
A reduced fraction a/d has gcd(a,d)=1; d=1 includes the two centers 0 and 1. Its first representative at q>=R is q_d=d*ceil(R/d).
The new remainder is asserted only for K>=max(6,2*R-2), so every d<R exception is already in the prefix.
Only scalar ambient measure is considered. No independence of the E_q, manifold restriction, matrix result, or parent solution is assumed or claimed.
approaches_considered: Discard nonprimitive pairs; falsified by missing low-denominator centers.
Reduce fractions retaining first multiples, then bound primitive tail counts using primes 2 and 3.
Use six residue classes and convex midpoint integration as an independent remainder envelope.
falsification_targets: Reduction preserves the lower denominator cutoff without exceptions.
The negative divisor terms may use upper integral bounds.
Scalar ambient nullity establishes a matrix-manifold result.

claims.statement: For every integer R>=2, group all scalar approximation intervals by reduced a/d and retain radius [d*ceil(R/d)]^-3. This preserves the full union; a finite prefix keeps exactly q_d<=K. Ordinary universal argument pending independent proof review.
